## Hands-on 4 – Exploring the menu {#hands-on-4-work-the-menu .smaller}

<!-- The methods deck submits the exploration to the class chart; the short
     session sends nothing. Keyed on the deck map in the YAML of each deck. -->

::: {.small}
**Task 4 is exploratory.** Try several specifications, look at what each one does, and get a feel for which decisions move the estimate.

1. Start from the reference: `try_spec()`
2. Change **one decision**, for example `try_spec(population = "all")`, and read the difference, its test and its place among the `r nrow(curve)`; `my_experiments()` lists every try
3. Do it again with a different decision. Three or four is plenty, and ask for one option that is off the curve, such as `try_spec(model = "three_group")`, to read why it is refused
4. Rerun the one that you can argue for best, so that it is your last try[, and **submit it** with `submit_exploration()`]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.methods"}
:::

::: {.fragment .small .content-visible when-meta="deck.methods"}
Your result appears on the live **Multiverse** page within seconds, as an open circle.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
[This is **not** your preregistered analysis.]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.methods"}[Nothing is sent anywhere.]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.methods"} You are allowed to look, change your mind and try again, which is why this phase has a name of its own.
:::

::: notes
This is where you get your hands properly dirty, and I want to be explicit about what kind of activity it is. Task 4 is exploration. Start from the reference with try underscore spec and no arguments, which gives the raw gap of the paper. Then change one decision and read what happens to the gap, its test and its place among the sixty-four. Every try is logged, and my underscore experiments lists them side by side.
